one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled event falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29: Q1 FY27 results come after the fiscal quarter ends Oct 31 (reported around late Nov/Dec 1), and the Sept 17 investor day already reaffirmed guidance unchanged. The stock has slid ~12% since the investor day ($303 on Sep 18 to $268) and sits ~6% above its 52-week low, so negative momentum and possible oversold reversal roughly offset. I therefore use a near-symmetric lognormal around $268 at monthly vol ~14% (50%/3.5), with a tiny drift adjustment making P(>=268) slightly under 50%. Macro prints (Sept CPI/jobs in mid-Oct) and software-sector AI headlines are the main swing factors.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (FY28E EPS incl. SBC ~$25.5 x 13x = $331, weight 0.6) and FCF-after-SBC yield (~$27/share NTM at Sept 2027 capitalised at 8% = $338, weight 0.4) gives ~$334 per share 12 months out.

INTU trades ~11.7x FY27 guided EPS today; its 10-yr TTM P/E range is 16-92x (median ~48x). reasoning: Facts: INTU fell ~62% in a year on agentic-AI disruption fears, a TurboTax slowdown (7% growth, price uncompetitive at low end), 3% online customer growth, a 17% workforce cut, and FY27 guidance of 9-10% revenue growth that missed consensus ($23.72B); the Sep 17 investor day merely reaffirmed guidance and the stock slid from $303 to $268. Yet the business still grows: FY26 revenue +14% to $21.4B, OCF $8.8B, $5.5B buybacks, and FY27 non-GAAP EPS (now including SBC) guided to $22.88-23.12, so the stock trades ~11.7x forward and near its 10-year P/E floor (~16x TTM). Base rates: (1) typical large-cap annual moves are +/-25-35%, this stock's realized vol is 50%, so I use sigma ~0.45; (2) large-cap tech names that crashed 40-65% in a de-rating while still growing earnings (META/CRM/ADBE/NFLX 2022) mostly rebounded strongly the next year, while genuine AI-disruption victims (Chegg 2023, -99% ultimately) kept falling as revenue shrank; INTU's still-growing revenue and EPS put it closer to the first group, but the 2026 software de-rating has persisted for ~9 months, so I only partly weight reversion; (3) the closest slow-growth comp, H&R Block, trades ~8-9x, a practical floor near $185-205 on FY27 EPS. Prediction markets: Polymarket ~35% US recession by end-2027 (Sept 24 2026; volume not retrievable, page blocked), Kalshi ~6% for rest-of-2026 - a modest left-tail add. Fair value blend ~$334; I set the distribution median at ~$288 (roughly 30% of the gap to fair value closed, plus buyback/EPS growth, offset by persistent negative momentum and narrative risk), lognormal sigma 0.45 with a slightly fatter left tail.
